analyst_view.overall: Leaders Almería (29 points, 24 scored and 10 conceded) host an Andorra side playing for the first time since the 2 November collision between their goalkeeper Jesús Owono and Tenerife's Jesús de Miguel, who died the next day. Coach Carles Manso said on Thursday the dressing room is still affected and the players have psychological support; Owono has not returned to training, and several reports agree his sanction has not yet been decided, so a replacement goalkeeper will play. Changed since the last view: the site no longer lists Lautaro De León or Efe Akman as suspended, and one report says Almería's Lopy is out and Chirino doubtful. No referee had been named when this was written.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. I still lean a little lower: Almería's last three league games were tight (1-0 at Girona, 1-1, 2-2) and they concede under a goal a game. Andorra's emotional state is the hardest thing to read; a stand-in goalkeeper is the main reason not to go lower.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners and I leave it. Both teams pass a lot (over 6,000 passes each by LaLiga's count), so Andorra may not simply sit deep, but Almería at home should still win most of the corners. The two effects broadly cancel out.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.7 cards, with Andorra expected to take 3.6. I lean lower: in their first match since the tragedy, I expect a careful game and a lenient tone, and Almería (25 yellows, the fewest of the two) have little reason to make it physical. Andorra's 205 fouls committed in 12 games are the risk to this lean.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots. I lean lower: Almería's win at Girona came from about 12 shots per side and LaLiga counts them at 130 shots in 13 games, ten a game. Andorra are more willing shooters (147 in 12), but a squad that has barely trained normally for a fortnight may not keep that up.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target, high for this division. I lean lower: Almería's recent games have been controlled rather than open, and Miguel de la Fuente (eight goals) tends to need few chances. If Andorra's replacement goalkeeper looks shaky, Almería may test him more, which is the main risk.
